school.tagged_body:
Needs or Wants?

Every day, we {{g:spend money on|spend + 돈 + on + 명사: ~에 돈을 쓰다}} many different things. But do you really need everything you buy? Stop and ask yourself this question.

{{v:Economists}} put the things we buy into two {{v:groups}}: {{v:needs}} and {{v:wants}}. Needs are things for living, like food, {{v:clothes}}, and {{g:a place to stay|to부정사 형용사적 용법: 머물 (장소)}}. We {{g:must have|must + 동사원형: ~해야 한다 (의무)}} them. Wants {{g:make life more fun or comfortable|make + 목적어 + 형용사: (목적어)를 ~하게 만들다}}, but we do not need them. New games, {{v:designer}} shoes, and {{v:the latest}} phone are wants.

You can buy things you want. That is OK. But {{t:there is a limit to our money, and there is no limit to our wants}}. {{v:Advertisements}} and {{v:social media}} {{g:make us feel|사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형: (목적어)가 ~하게 하다}}, "I need something new!" {{g:If we spend too much money on wants|조건의 if: 만약 ~라면 (미래의 일도 현재시제)}}, we may not have {{v:enough}} money for our needs or for the {{v:future}}.

So {{t:you should make a budget}}. A {{v:budget}} is a {{v:plan}} for your money. It shows {{g:how much money you will spend and save|간접의문문: how much + 명사 + 주어 + 동사}}. Here is one {{v:helpful}} {{v:tip}}: the "24-hour {{v:rule}}." Sometimes you want to buy something, but it is not a need. Then {{g:wait for 24 hours|명령문: 동사원형으로 시작 / for + 기간: ~ 동안}} before you buy it. Often, you {{g:will not really want it anymore|not ~ anymore: 더 이상 ~하지 않다}}.

You should {{g:learn to manage|learn + to부정사: ~하는 것을 배우다}} money {{v:wisely}}. {{t:This skill will help you for the rest of your life}}.

{{v:Economists}} {{v:divide}} the things we buy into two {{v:groups}}: {{v:needs}} and {{v:wants}}. Needs are things {{g:that we must have to live|목적격 관계대명사 that + to부정사 부사적 용법(목적): 살기 위해 꼭 가져야 하는}}, such as food, {{v:clothes}}, and a place to stay. Wants are things {{g:that make life more fun or comfortable|주격 관계대명사 that + make + 목적어 + 형용사}} but are not {{v:necessary}}, such as new games, {{v:designer}} shoes, or {{v:the latest}} phone.

{{g:It is not wrong to buy things we want|가주어 it, 진주어 to부정사: ~하는 것은 잘못이 아니다}}. {{t:The problem is that our money is limited, but our wants are not}}. {{v:Advertisements}} and {{v:social media}} {{g:make us feel|사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형: (목적어)가 ~하게 하다}} that we always need something new. If we spend too much money on wants, we may not have {{v:enough}} for our needs or for the {{v:future}}.

{{g:That is why|That is why + 주어 + 동사: 그래서 ~하다}} {{g:making a budget is important|동명사 주어: making ~ (단수 취급 → is)}}. A {{v:budget}} is a plan {{g:that shows|주격 관계대명사 that: 앞의 a plan을 꾸민다}} how much money you will spend and {{v:save}}. One {{v:helpful}} {{v:tip}} is the "24-hour {{v:rule}}." When you want to buy something that is not a need, wait for 24 hours {{g:before buying it|전치사 before + 동명사: ~하기 전에}}. Often, you will find that you don't really want it {{v:anymore}}.

essays.q: Summarize the passage in three English sentences: (1) the distinction between needs and wants, (2) the central problem, and (3) the proposed solutions.
essays.sampleAnswer: Economists categorize purchases into needs, which are indispensable to survival, and wants, which enhance enjoyment but are by no means essential. The central problem is that our financial resources are finite while our wants are virtually limitless, and advertisements make us feel perpetually in need of something new. To address this, the writer recommends establishing a budget and postponing non-essential purchases for 24 hours.

essays.q: Do you think the 24-hour rule is effective for teenagers? Give your opinion and suggest one more way to manage money wisely in 3–4 English sentences.
essays.sampleAnswer: I think the 24-hour rule is effective for teenagers because many of our purchases are impulsive. After waiting a day, we can think more clearly about whether we really need something. Another good way is to save a fixed amount of money every week before spending any. This habit helps us prepare for the future.
